input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: style() tests fg and bg for truthiness instead of `is not None`, so the 256-color index 0 is skipped
- failure path: click.style('x', fg=0) or bg=0, meaning black, applies no color at all and the text renders in the terminal default; the caller sees no error

Reviewer finding
- description: The truthiness checks skip color index 0 for both foreground and background.
- rationale: Calling style("text", fg=0) or style("text", bg=0) now skips the corresponding ANSI sequence because 0 is falsy. Index 0 is a valid palette color, so text uses the terminal's existing color instead of the requested black.
critique: The finding names the same mechanism as the label: truthiness checks on fg/bg treat the 256-color index 0 as falsy. As a result, style('text', fg=0) or bg=0 emits no ANSI code and the text renders in the default color instead of black.
